This was eighth season of J1 League as renamed from J. League Division 1. [[Kawasaki Frontale]] were the defending champions, having won their fourth and second consecutive title in [[2021 J1 League|2021]] with four rounds to play.{{cite web|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/sport/football/football-kawasaki-retain-japanese-title-despite-late-urawa-equaliser|work=The Straits Times|date=3 November 2021|title=Football: Kawasaki retain Japanese title despite late Urawa equaliser}} [[Yokohama F. Marinos]] reclaimed the trophy, winning its fifth J.League and seventh [[List of Japanese football champions|Japanese]] title on the final day of the season.{{cite web |title=We created history: Muscat follows in the footsteps of Postecoglou to win the J1 League!|url=https://keepup.com.au/news/muscat-follows-in-the-footsteps-of-postecoglou-to-win-the-j1-league|website=KeepUp.com.au|publisher=Australian Professional Leagues Company |access-date=8 November 2022 |date=5 November 2022|first=Sacha|last=Pisani}}{{cite web |title=Yokohama F. Marinos win fifth J1 title after tense battle on season's last day|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2022/11/05/soccer/j-league/j1-champions-fmarinos/|website=The Japan Times|access-date=8 November 2022 |date=5 November 2022|first=Dan|last=Orlowitz}} Brazilian forward [[Thiago Santana]] scored 14 goals for [[Shimizu S-Pulse]], the least number of goals from a player who became the [[J.League Top Scorer|league top scorer]] and the first to also suffer relegation in the same season. ==Overview== Due to [[2022 FIFA World Cup]], the league began from February to November 2022. ==Changes from the previous season== There were four teams instead of two relegated last season to [[2022 J2 League]] due to [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on association football|impacts]] related to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|COVID-19 pandemic]] to made up the decision of no relegation in the [[2020 J1 League|2020 season]],{{Cite web|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2020/03/19/soccer/j-league/j-league-skip-relegation-schedule-threatened-coronavirus/|title=J. League to skip relegation as schedule threatened by coronavirus|first=Dan|last=Orlowitz|date=19 March 2020|website=The Japan Times}} which saw the number of teams rise to 20.{{cite press release|title=Number of clubs promoted and relegated at the end of the 2021 season|url=https://www.jleague.jp/sp/en/news/article/18415|publisher=Japan Professional Football League|website=JLeague.jp|date=18 November 2020|access-date=18 November 2020|archive-date=16 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201216091635/https://www.jleague.jp/sp/en/news/article/18415/|url-status=dead}} They were [[Tokushima Vortis]], [[Oita Trinita]], [[Vegalta Sendai]], and [[Yokohama FC]]. ==Promotion–relegation playoffs== In the playoffs, officially called the 2022 J.League J1/J2 Play-offs ({{langx|ja|2022 J1参入プレーオフ}}), the 16th-placed team of the J1 League ([[Kyoto Sanga FC|Kyoto Sanga]]) faced the winners of the J2 League promotion playoffs. Should they lose, the J2 team would be promoted in their place for the 2023 J1 League. [[Fagiano Okayama]], [[Roasso Kumamoto]], [[Oita Trinita]], and [[Montedio Yamagata]] qualified for the promotion playoffs as they finished between third and sixth in the [[2022 J2 League]]. In the first two rounds of the playoffs, if the score was tied after 90 minutes, no extra time was played and the winners were the team with the higher finish in the J2 League (i.e. the home team).
